description:
## What the code does

Across calendars-client, every `properties: Option<&[&str]>` argument is serialised to a JSON array via a hand-rolled iterator chain:

```rust
// crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs:38-41
if let Some(props) = properties {
    args["properties"] = serde_json::Value::Array(
        props.iter().copied().map(serde_json::Value::from).collect(),
    );
}
```

The same six-line pattern is repeated **six times**:

- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs:38-41
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event.rs:37-40
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event_notification.rs:30-33
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event_parse.rs:30-33
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/participant_identity.rs:25-28
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/principal_availability.rs:36-39

## What idiomatic Rust would do

`serde_json::to_value` on `&[&str]` invokes the `str` Serialize impl on each element and produces `Value::Array(Vec<Value::String>)` — byte-identical wire output to the hand-rolled version. The two-line replacement:

```rust
if let Some(props) = properties {
    args["properties"] = serde_json::to_value(props)
        .expect("&[&str] Serialize is infallible");
}
```

…matches the idiom the SAME function uses two lines above for the `ids` slice:

```rust
// calendar.rs:35-36 — already in the idiomatic shape
if let Some(id_slice) = ids {
    args["ids"] = serde_json::to_value(id_slice).expect("Id slice Serialize is infallible");
}
```

## Why it matters

1. **Local consistency.** The function asks the reader to recognise two different idioms for the same operation (slice → JSON array) two lines apart in the same function. Picking one and using it throughout is what a serious Rust practitioner would do without thinking.

2. **Maintainability.** Six copies of the same hand-rolled chain means six opportunities for one of them to drift (e.g. someone adds `.filter()` to one site, the others diverge). One canonical idiom = zero divergence.

3. **Composability.** `serde_json::to_value` is the workspace's standard "value of T into wire-Value" helper; using it consistently keeps a future refactor (e.g. converting `properties: Option<&[&str]>` to a typed `Option<&[CalendarProperty]>`) trivial — the same call site works because `CalendarProperty: Serialize`.

4. **Canonical-template alignment.** The canonical mail-client `email_get` at email.rs:44-48 has the same hand-rolled pattern (likely because the workspace's earliest version had it and the cookie-cut propagated it). Per workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template rule, fixing it here means fixing the canonical first; that's a separate (and welcome) propagation sweep. The finding here is calendars-specific because that's the scope of this review epic.

## Fix shape

Six mechanical two-line replacements. Wire output unchanged. Cookie-cutter consistency improves.

## Source citations

- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs:38-41 (and matching :35-36 for the canonical idiom in the same function)
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event.rs:37-40
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event_notification.rs:30-33
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event_parse.rs:30-33
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/participant_identity.rs:25-28
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/principal_availability.rs:36-39
- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:44-48 (canonical — same hand-rolled pattern; canonical-template propagation candidate)
